theory.intro: To find the regular payment needed to reach a savings goal or pay off a loan, divide the target value by the interest factor from the table: $M = \dfrac{\text{Target Value}}{\text{Factor}}$. These tables assume payments are made at the end of each compounding period.
facts: For a future savings goal $\text{FV}$, the required regular contribution is $M = \dfrac{\text{FV}}{\text{FV factor}}$.
For a loan or pension fund of present value $\text{PV}$, the regular payment is $M = \dfrac{\text{PV}}{\text{PV factor}}$.
Always convert the annual rate to the **periodic rate** $r$ and years to the **number of periods** $n$.
Total interest paid on a loan is $\text{Interest} = (n \times M) - \text{PV}$.
Round the payment to the nearest cent or nearest dollar as requested. When calculating total repayments, use the rounded payment requested in the question.
steps: Find the rate per period $r$ and total number of periods $n$.
Read the appropriate interest factor from the table at $(n, r)$.
Divide the future value or present value by the interest factor: $M = \dfrac{\text{Value}}{\text{Factor}}$.
Multiply $n \times M$ and subtract $\text{PV}$ if loan interest is requested.

workedExamples.question_text:
Amira wants to save $\$18\,000$ in three years by making equal deposits at the end of each quarter. Her account pays $10\%$ p.a. compounded quarterly.
The table shows future value interest factors for an annuity of $\$1$ per period.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline n & 2\% & 2.5\% \\ \hline 8 & 8.5830 & 8.7361 \\ 12 & 13.4121 & 13.7956 \\ \hline \end{array}$
Use the table to calculate the required quarterly contribution, to the nearest cent.

Ravi invests $\$180\,000$ in an account paying $6\%$ p.a. compounded monthly. He will make equal withdrawals at the end of each month for 15 years, exhausting the account.
The table shows present value interest factors for an annuity of $\$1$ per period.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline n & 0.5\% & 0.6\% \\ \hline 120 & 90.0735 & 85.3666 \\ 180 & 118.5035 & 109.8845 \\ \hline \end{array}$
Use the table to calculate his monthly income, to the nearest cent.

Ella borrows $\$24\,000$ over five years at $7.2\%$ p.a. compounded monthly. Repayments are made at the end of each month.
The table shows present value interest factors for an annuity of $\$1$ per period.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline n & 0.5\% & 0.6\% \\ \hline 48 & 42.5803 & 41.5988 \\ 60 & 51.7256 & 50.2621 \\ \hline \end{array}$
a. Calculate the monthly repayment, to the nearest cent.
b. Use this rounded repayment to calculate the total amount repaid.
c. Calculate the total interest paid.
workedExamples.solution_text:
a.
$\begin{aligned}r&=\frac{7.2\%}{12}=0.6\%\\n&=5\times12=60\end{aligned}$
The present value factor is $50.2621$.
$\begin{aligned}24\,000&=50.2621M\\M&=\frac{24\,000}{50.2621}\\&=\$477.50\end{aligned}$
b.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Total repaid}&=60\times477.50\\&=\$28\,650.00\end{aligned}$
c.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Interest}&=28\,650-24\,000\\&=\$4650.00\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text:
Noah buys a car for $\$28\,000$ and pays a $10\%$ deposit. He borrows the remaining amount over four years at $9\%$ p.a. compounded monthly, making repayments at the end of each month.
The table shows present value interest factors for an annuity of $\$1$ per period.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline n & 0.7\% & 0.75\% \\ \hline 48 & 40.64856 & 40.18478 \\ \hline \end{array}$
a. Calculate the monthly repayment, to the nearest dollar.
b. Use this rounded repayment to calculate the total interest paid over the loan term.
workedExamples.solution_text:
a.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Deposit}&=0.10\times28\,000=\$2800\\\text{Principal}&=28\,000-2800=\$25\,200\\r&=\frac{9\%}{12}=0.75\%\\n&=4\times12=48\end{aligned}$
The present value factor is $40.18478$.
$\begin{aligned}M&=\frac{25\,200}{40.18478}\\&\approx\$627.10\end{aligned}$
The monthly repayment is $\$627$ to the nearest dollar.
b.
$\begin{aligned}\text{Total repaid}&=48\times627=\$30\,096\\\text{Interest}&=30\,096-25\,200\\&=\$4896\end{aligned}$

workedExamples.question_text:
Mia borrows $\$12\,000$ over four years, making equal repayments at the end of each month. She compares two loans charging $7.2\%$ p.a. and $4.8\%$ p.a., both compounded monthly.
The table shows present value interest factors for an annuity of $\$1$ per period.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline n & 0.4\% & 0.6\% \\ \hline 48 & 43.5942 & 41.5988 \\ \hline \end{array}$
Calculate the monthly repayment at each rate, to the nearest cent. Use these rounded repayments to calculate the total repaid at each rate and the amount saved by choosing the lower rate.
